To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we measured the single spin asymmetry of $\pi^0-$ production at 50 GeV in the polarized proton target fragmentation region and found the asymmetry to be in agreement with measurements carried out at higher energy.

the single spin asymmetries in the polarized proton and target fragmentation regions are of similar magnitude and opposite in sign, which is in contradiction to the predictions of the naive twist-3 approach.

the spin asymmetries in the polarized proton fragmentation region were measured at different energies and are in agreement with predictions of theoretical models, and the single spin asymmetry in $\pi^0-$meson production in the polarized neutron fragmentation region was measured at 50 GeV for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of spin effects in high energy hadronic reactions.
the study of hadron production in high-energy interactions.
the study of spin effects in the fragmentation process and in the hadronization mechanism in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin-dependent part of the fragmentation function is not universal, but it has a significant energy dependence.
the single spin asymmetry in the polarized proton target fragmentation region is a function of the energy, $x_F$ and $P_t$ and that it is in agreement with the Sivers effect.
the spin asymmetry in pion production in the polarized proton fragmentation region has been measured over a wide energy and momentum transfer range, and the results are in agreement with each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polarized measurements at PROZA setup have been very successful.

we have shown that the single spin asymmetry in the polarized proton fragmentation region is a universal function of the transverse momentum of the produced hadron, and the function is independent of the energy and the type of the produced hadrons.
we have been able to study the spin asymmetry in the polarized fragmentation region in the energy range 5-50 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetry in polarized target fragmentation is in agreement with the asymmetry in the polarized proton fragmentation region.

the single-spin asymmetries are energy independent and that the energy independence is related to the fact that the asymmetries are determined by the transverse momentum distribution of the produced hadrons.
the single-spin asymmetries in $\pi^0, \eta$ production in proton-proton collisions at 50 and 200 GeV energies are consistent with each other.
